_doc: Documented, intentional legacy -> migrated behaviour changes, consumed by parity/diff.py. A flow is only classified INTENTIONAL DIFFERENCE when every functional field that differs from legacy is listed in `expect_migrated` and the migrated response matches it exactly; any other deviation from legacy is a REGRESSION.

F02.root_cause: The JSP login page was replaced by the React SPA. The backend keeps /redirect as a legacy-compat route that 302s to the SPA sign-in page (/signin), which the nginx front door serves with 200 (verified by parity/probes.sh).

F01.root_cause: GET / still answers 302, but the target is the SPA sign-in route /signin instead of the JSP /redirect page. Same user outcome: an anonymous visitor lands on the login form.

F05.root_cause: Legacy forwarded a failed login to the JSP login page (200). Migrated uses Post/Redirect/Get: 302 to /signin?error. Same outcome: no token, no cookie, back on the login form. Known limitation: the React sign-in page does not read ?error yet, so a failed legacy-style form POST shows the empty form without an error banner (the SPA's own JSON sign-in does show one).

F06.root_cause: Same Post/Redirect/Get change as F05. Unknown users and wrong passwords stay indistinguishable (same redirect; AuthService burns one BCrypt check for unknown users so timing does not leak either).

F07.root_cause: Legacy silently fell through to the login page when email/password were missing. Migrated redirects to /signin without ?error (nothing was attempted). No token, no cookie.

F09.root_cause: Password comparison is still case-sensitive (PARISDKH rejected); only the failure transport changed (Post/Redirect/Get, see F05).

F10.root_cause: Legacy built HQL by string concatenation (FROM com.schema.User U WHERE U.username='...'), so a quote produced org.hibernate.QueryException and the exception text was returned to the client (injection surface + information leak). Migrated looks the user up by primary key through Spring Data JPA (bound parameter) and treats it as an ordinary failed login.

F11.root_cause: Injection payload is rejected on both sides (legacy happened to fail the plaintext compare). Migrated uses a bound parameter and the Post/Redirect/Get failure transport (see F05).

F15.root_cause: Legacy GET /token minted a signed admin JWT for the hard-coded user 'tarangparikh' to any unauthenticated caller (privilege-escalation defect). Migrated /token only re-issues a token for a caller that already presents a valid JWT (cookie or Bearer) and returns RFC 7807 401 otherwise.

F16.root_cause: Spring Security is deny-by-default: unauthenticated requests to any non-public path get 401 before routing, so anonymous callers cannot enumerate routes. An authenticated request to /nonexistent returns 404 (verified by parity/probes.sh), and the nginx front door serves the SPA for unknown browser routes.

jwt.signature_len.root_cause: Legacy signs with the RSA-1024 private key committed to the repo (WEB-INF/StoredObject/system.key; 171-char RS256 signature). Migrated generates a per-environment RSA-2048 key pair at first start (jwt-keys service; 342-char signature). Algorithm (RS256), claims and TTL are unchanged; tokens are not interchangeable between the estates.

cookie.JSESSIONID.root_cause: Legacy Tomcat creates an HTTP session (JSESSIONID) on JSP/servlet requests. The migrated API is stateless (SessionCreationPolicy.STATELESS); the only auth state is the JWT 'token' cookie / Bearer header.
